description.narrative:
Sekretariatet för Södra Afrikas utvecklingsgemenskap (SADC) har lämnat in ett förslag till stöd för ett projekt som syftar till att påskynda genomförandet av SADC:s strategi för SRHR för att säkerställa att människor i SADC-regionen har god sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter. Projektet pågår mellan 2025 och 2028.
SADC:s strategi för SRHR är ett regionalt godkänt dokument som vägleder medlemsländernas arbete för förbättrad SRHR fram till 2030. Sekretariatets roll är att samordna insatserna och ge tekniskt stöd till medlemsstaterna för att uppnå de mål och delmål som anges i strategin. SADC-sekretariatets kapacitet är dock för närvarande begränsad för att kunna ta på sig den roll som krävs på grund av begränsade resurser. Det föreslagna projektet syftar därför till att adressera utmaningar och öka kapaciteten så att sekretariatet fullt ut kan anta sin förvaltningsroll och stödja medlemsstaterna i genomförandet av strategin för sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter.

The Secretariat of the Southern Africa Development Community (SADC) has submitted a proposal for support for a project that aims to fast-track the implementation of the SADC SRHR Strategy to ensure that people in the SADC region have good sexual and reproductive health and rights. The project period is between 2025 to 2028.
The SADC SRHR Strategy is a regionally approved document, guiding the member states' work towards improved SRHR up to 2030. The Secretariat's role is to coordinate efforts and provide technical assistance to member states to achieve the targets and milestones as per the strategy. However, the SADC Secretariat capacity is currently constrained to assume the required stewardship role due to limited resources. The proposed project therefore seeks to address bottlenecks and boost capacity so that the Secretariat fully can assume its stewardship role and support member states in the implementation of the SRHR Strategy.

The project will contribute to the SADC SRHR Strategy vision/goal, which is to 'Ensure that all people enjoy a healthy sexual and reproductive life, have sustainable access, coverage and quality SRHR services, information and education and are able to fully realize and exercise their SRH rights, as integral to sustainable human development in SADC'.
This will be achieved through four objectives:
1. To enhance leadership and stewardship capabilities for an inclusive-comprehensive multi-sectoral SRHR response at the SADC Secretariat and Member States. This includes strengthening stewardship responsibilities and social accountability of the state to create an enabling environment with sufficient financial and technical resources and materials required to accelerate efforts to realise SRHR outcomes and targets in SADC.
2. To support the domestication and implementation of global and regional (AU and SADC) policy commitments and human rights standards in Member States. This entails providing technical and capacity building support to Member States to translate international frameworks and best practices on health promotion and SRHR into national policies, strategies and programs that deliver services to all citizens who need them indiscriminately.
3. To strengthen Member States' health and social systems to inclusively deliver integrated and comprehensive SRHR service packages for Universal Health Coverage. In particular, the project will provide technical support to strengthen national health service delivery systems and promote holistic approaches to deliver integrated SRHR/GBV/HIV services for all people, including among children and young people, and in humanitarian and emergency situations.
4. To strengthen integrated-multi-sectoral SRHR Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting (MER) that inform improved decision making, policies and programming at SADC Secretariat and in Member States. This will entail support towards strengthening data driven and evidence-based national monitoring and evaluation systems. It will also entail support to Member States' reporting on the SRHR Strategy and the benefits derived from implementing the SADC SRHR Strategy in the region.
